claims: Eid al-Fitr is also known as the "Festival of Breaking the Fast".
Eid al-Fitr is a three-day Islamic holiday.
Eid al-Fitr marks the end of Ramadan’s month-long dawn-to-sunset fasting.
Eid al-Fitr begins upon the first sighting of the new crescent moon.
"Eid" means "festival" or "feast".
"Fitr" refers to "breaking the fast".
Eid al-Fitr occurs at the start of Shawwal.
Shawwal is the 10th month of the Islamic (Hijri) calendar.
The exact date of Eid al-Fitr changes annually based on the lunar calendar and the sighting of the crescent moon.
Muslims gather in mosques or open areas for special morning prayers on the first day of Eid al-Fitr.
It is mandatory to give Zakat al-Fitr to the poor and needy before the prayers.
People wear new clothes during Eid al-Fitr.
People visit family and friends during Eid al-Fitr.
People exchange greetings of "Eid Mubarak" during Eid al-Fitr.
"Eid Mubarak" means "Blessed Eid".
Special meals and sweets are shared during Eid al-Fitr.
Children often receive gifts or money known as Eidi during Eid al-Fitr.
Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha.
Eid al-Adha is known as the "Festival of Sacrifice".
Eid al-Adha occurs about two months after Eid al-Fitr.
Eid al-Adha occurs during the Hajj pilgrimage.
